text:
maria: heads-up — noticed a sharp latency/regression on the MoE routing path in nightly perf tests, appears to be all-to-all hotspots on 8xA100 setups. raw traces attached in the dashboard: https://dash.redwood/prof/1245 :eyes:

alex: saw this too. p50 up ~25% and p99 worse. regression started after the kernel-selection change last week (fallback to non-fused GEMM for small hidden dims).

sam: curious if it's comm or compute. I pulled an nsys capture — top wait is all-to-all + cudaMemcpy. excerpt: 
```
Timeline: 0-100ms
compute kernels 35ms
alltoall 28ms
cudaMemcpy (pinned) 22ms
other sync 15ms
```
Flame looks like routing fanout sizes jumped for a subset of tokens.

ben: also saw uneven expert fanout distribution in telemetry. small # of tokens fanout->hundreds of experts -> giant all-to-all messages. KV cache stats show repeated misses for those keys (cache-miss spike coincident with regression).

lina: hmm that could amplify all-to-all. if KV cache misses force full prefix recompute we end up with massive token fanout + repeated memcopies. any chance batching heuristics changed? we recently widened the batching window to 12ms.

maria: yes batching window bumped in the same release. hypothesis: widened window mixed diverse seq lengths and routing patterns -> larger variance in fanout -> hot all-to-all sizes -> NCCL algorithm not ideal -> stalls.

alex: repro plan: 1) run small window (2ms) + original kernel selection 2) force local-expert-prefetch (experimental) 3) pin NCCL algorithm to tree/ ring vs tree-based autotune.

sam: quick commands I used: 
```
# collect perf
nsys profile --output=moe_reg /bin/python -m tests.moerun
# torchprof snippet
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
export NCCL_ALGO=ring
export TORCH_NVFUSER_DISABLE=1
```

ben: added a lightweight telemetry dump (paste): 
```
route_stats: {
  median_fanout: 4,
  99p_fanout: 112,
  fanout_cv: 2.8
}
kv_cache: { hit_rate: 0.73, miss_spike_count: 17 }
alltoall: { p95_time: 45ms, p99_time: 112ms }
```

lina: that 99p_fanout is brutal. even with efficient alltoall, packing/unpacking cost + many small messages kills perf. we should try grouping experts by device affinity to reduce cross-device fanout.

maria: action items proposed: 
- rollback batching window to 4ms and run nightly sweep
- test kernel-selection flag (force fused matmul where possible)
- enable KV prefetch for hot keys + throttle expert swap frequency
- experiment with NCCL_ALGO=ring vs tree and TORCH_NCCL_SYNC_ALLREDUCE=1 for overlap tuning

alex: I'll run two scaled runs on staging (8xA100) with: 
```
BATCH_WINDOW_MS=4
FORCE_FUSED_GEMM=1
EXPERT_PREFETCH=1
NCCL_ALGO=ring
```
ETA ~2 hours.

deploy-bot: scheduled run on staging cluster (8x-a100-01): job id moe-reg-2063456790 (started).

sam: small note — the kernel-selection fallback was introduced because fused matmul regresses for seq_len>2048 on tensor-parallel shards due to an indexing bug. if we force fused we may re-hit that bug. need guard rails and a quick unit test.

ben: good call. maybe instead of forcing fused globally, add route-size heuristic: if expected fanout > 32, prefer fused path; else use conservative kernels. this flips selection based on routing fanout distribution.

lina: we can approximate expected fanout from token prefix stats in the router; add a cheap estimator in selection logic. should be low overhead.

maria: noted. prioritize the batching rollback + expert-prefetch experiment first to get signal. if that helps we'll iterate on kernel selection heuristics with a small unit test harness to exercise the long-seq path.

alex: quick update — run 1 complete. p50 improved, p99 down ~30%. alltoall p99 reduced to ~70ms. looks promising. uploading traces: https://dash.redwood/prof/1246

sam: great. can you diff the nvtx spans to see overlap changes (compute vs memcpy)?

alex: diff shows ~12ms more compute overlap, and memcpy shifted to earlier prefetch stage (less critical path).

ben: thanks — setting followups: kernel-selection feature flag ticket, router-estimator PR, and telemetry alert for 99p_fanout > 64. filing infra tickets.

maria: awesome. please paste the job ids and attach PR links here when ready. i'll add to the release notes and rollback notes for the change that introduced the batching window bump. :thumbsup:

lina: leaving a note — consider a long-term plan to shard experts by affinity and prepartition all-to-all into fewer bigger messages (pack) to reduce NCCL overhead. but that's a larger architecture change.

maria: agreed. for now we have a mitigation path. thanks team.

alex: I'll drop the perf captures + a minimal repro in the PR: https://git.redwood/p/moe/merge/578

deploy-bot: job moe-reg-2063456790 finished: success.

ben: assigning followups: MOE-247 (kernel heuristic), MOE-248 (router estimator), MOE-249 (telemetry alert).

maria: great work. closing thread unless new regressions show up. :sparkles:
